runtime: Actual production-built dashboard and local Worker/D1/DO/R2/KV; production OpenConnector HTTP adapter. No frontend extension stubs or backend HTTP interception.
fixtureScope: Disposable synthetic OpenConnector metadata/OAuth account service only. Consent screens are fixture forms with no real vendor, account, credential, terms, purchase, message or action.
authentication: One genuine disposable local first-owner signup in the initial run, followed by real sign-ins to the same account; no seeded or additional operator account.
limitations: No deployed Cloudflare or real vendor acceptance.
No positive browser multi-owner proof; separate production-adapter real-HTTP test covers two-owner isolation.
Blocked-popup case deliberately injects window.open returning null; it tests the real UI failure path, not browser permission policy.
No provider inference, containers, MCP network success, external messages or purchases.

checks.name: Fresh auth-safe tree denies anonymous whoami, sessions, skills, workspaces and app accounts401; forged default identity headers gain no authority.
Fresh tree blocked-popup fault is actionable and produces no authorization call (controlled window.open(null) injection).
Fresh tree synthetic authorization503 closes the popup and creates no app account.
Fresh tree explicit synthetic denial returns to retryable state with no account or employee permissions.
Fresh tree actual success-shaped callback and completion hints do not establish consent without the matching owned generation.
Fresh built UI: Disconnect -> Browse -> explicit synthetic Allow shows verified success rather than stale disconnected notice.
Fresh built UI: inline Connect app also clears stale notice and confirms only the new exact owned generation.
Fresh build preserves prior real skill activation/disable and reviewed founder import: disabled template reinstallable, founder bot archived, instructions draft, Deploy409.
Actual canonical MCP UI rejects local HTTP with403 destination_not_trusted and leaves registry empty; public HTTPS guard unchanged.
Actual sign-out removes session access: app accounts and skills401, with no cached account visible.
